proposed_fixes.title: Validate and recover unresolved network Dock pins
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Likely mismatch between persisted widget-page IDs and the provider's advertised Dock-band IDs. This is supported by repeated lookup failures, but the origin of the pin and the necessity of a legacy alias are not yet established.
plan: Reproduce current Network and Network Speed bands on 0.102.3001, then seed network_widget and gpu_widget pins in an isolated profile.
Trace pin creation/restoration through provider band enumeration and DockViewModel.SetupBands; verify whether any supported older build wrote these exact IDs.

If a supported legacy alias is confirmed, migrate it to the equivalent advertised band ID while preserving position and avoiding duplicate bands. Do not silently map Network utilization to Network Speed.
If the IDs were never supported as bands, reject invalid pin creation and expose an explicit repair/re-add path rather than silently dropping the item.
Add focused pin-restore/restart tests for current, legacy/invalid and duplicate pins; leave network sampling unchanged.
verification: A newly added Network or Network Speed band appears after restart.
The confirmed affected pin is either safely migrated once or visibly repairable; repeated startups do not duplicate or silently remove unrelated bands.
No unsupported-command warnings remain for a successfully repaired network pin; disabled-provider placeholders still behave correctly.

confidence.rationale: The reporter's actual lookup errors match released ID definitions exactly; pin provenance and a controlled reproduction have not been established.

reproduce.title: Compare current Network band with unresolved widget pin
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.102.3001, then current main if needed
prerequisites: Use disposable test data; preserve existing user configuration
setup: Use an isolated Dock profile, not the reporter's full settings.
Record an ordinary working Network/Network Speed pin before changing test configuration.
steps: 1. Enable Performance Monitor and add its advertised Network band through Dock customization; restart Command Palette and record visibility.
2. In a separate disposable profile, configure provider PerformanceMonitor with command com.microsoft.cmdpal.network_widget; restart and compare resolution.
3. Repeat with the advertised performanceWidget.network and performanceWidget.networkSpeed IDs and check for duplicate pins and startup ordering.
4. Establish whether a supported upgrade path creates the unresolved ID; choose migration only if that provenance is confirmed.
reproduce.expected_result: Current advertised bands resolve and display. An invalid or legacy pin has a deterministic repair path rather than disappearing without explanation.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare separate disposable Dock profiles for an advertised Network band and the known unresolved widget-page ID. Do not alter live Dock settings or request another full report.

fix_assessment.rationale: A focused Dock pin-resolution correction is plausible. Existing performance-card redesigns do not establish coverage of the specific unresolved pin; no competing implementation of this precise path was found.
